assignedTask.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
assignedTask.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.

Parent: [#402](https://github.com/brianreborn/familia/issues/402) (Security focus for 0.3.0). Target: `main`. Unassigned so the swarm can claim. Suggested owners: Boundary Reviewer (tool policy, including residual TR-3/TR-4), Covert Channel Reviewer/Fixer (injection via tool results, egress), Platform Reviewer (inventory of what is actually wired).

## Context

What familia wires today (inventory starting point, not complete):

- Agent-Reach: menu `reach.mcp` runs `scripts/agent_reach.py mcp-example` and prints `mcpServers` JSON for llama UI / code-bootstraps.
- Hermes / graph: `scripts/hermes_harness.py`, `server_tools` on nodes. Some planned nodes use `server_tools: all`; guardian/pentest nodes stay empty (TOOLS-005 fail-closed). DESIGN.md: the existing approval gate still guards shell and MCP.
- Auth env: `API_KEY_FILE`, `FAMILIA_API_KEY`, `LLAMA_API_KEY` (see `docs/api-key-design.md`, `scripts/familia_auth.py`). #394 is a test KeyError on `GITHUB_TOKEN` under FreeBSD.
- Already fixed, do not re-open as new bugs: H4 (read-only tools by default after #292), #345 (off-loopback direct tools; closed).

Residual product gaps with tests already on `main` (strict xfails in `tests/test_routing_toolroute_boundary.py` after #364 / [#362](https://github.com/brianreborn/familia/pull/362)). No public issue had been filed for these, so they live here rather than as a fifth tracker:

- TR-3 residual: `normalize_role` does NFKC + casefold but does not `strip()` or drop Unicode format characters (category Cf, e.g. U+200B). Padded or lookalike fail-closed role names (`guardian` / `pentest` / `defender`) become unknown TYPEs, so tools can be forwarded. Case and fullwidth variants were already tightened in #362.
- TR-4: a node-level `role: coder` (or other tool-capable type) can override a fail-closed model role, so a guardian model can be relabelled into a tool-forward path.

Related: green-roomz #43 (default-deny egress, research only), #236 leftover L14/L15.

- [ ] Inventory MCP servers and tools familia actually wires (Agent-Reach, Hermes server tools, llama-ui mcpServers, any code-bootstraps hook). Table: name, who launches it, default permission, network egress, whether it sees env secrets. Do not dump env values.

inboundFeedback.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
inboundFeedback.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.
